fem_toolbox.solvers.piezo_dynamics.documentation:
Small-model Tet4/Tet10 piezo modal reference with algebraic electric DOFs.

The dense Schur reference is intentionally limited to 2048 active [u, phi]
DOFs. No electric mass, artificial grounding, or dynamic thermal feedback.

PiezoelectricModes.documentation:
Mass-normalized real eigenvectors in sorted active-node order.

Arrays: displacement (nmodes,nactive,3), potential (nmodes,nactive),
angular_frequencies (nmodes,) rad/s, frequencies_hz (nmodes,) Hz.
Modal amplitudes satisfy u.T M u=1 (SI mass metric); they are shapes,
not a physical displacement/voltage excitation. The largest mechanical
component is positive. Degenerate eigenspaces have no unique basis.
Electrical residuals are evaluated after tying conducting electrodes;
conductor charge is minus the sum of original electrical residuals.
All arrays are owned immutable snapshots. No experimental validation.

solve_piezoelectric_modes.parameters: mesh: Mesh, material: PiezoelectricMaterial | Sequence[PiezoelectricMaterial], density: ArrayLike, conditions: Iterable[Dirichlet], *, backend: LinearBackend | None=None, count: int=6, electrodes: Sequence[Electrode] | None=None
solve_piezoelectric_modes.documentation:
Solve the lowest ``count`` supported, undamped natural modes.

``backend`` is an experimental linear-backend hook; None selects SciPy.
Reduction, physical residuals and result units remain this solver's contract.

Constant density: positive scalar or (ncells,) kg/m³. Dirichlet indices
use piezoelectric_dofs(mesh); all prescribed values/charges must be zero
(homogeneous perturbations). Electrode(potential=0) is shorted to the
reference, Electrode(charge=0) is a floating equipotential open circuit.
Every connected component needs an explicit potential reference and
supports eliminating rigid-body modes. Uncovered electric boundaries
have D.n=0; these are not automatically conducting electrodes.

Only mechanical DOFs carry consistent Tet4/Tet10 mass. Eliminate free electric
DOFs via K_eff=Kuu+B D^-1 B.T, then solve K_eff u=omega² M u using a
symmetric definite eigensolver. Reconstruct phi=D^-1 B.T u. The dense
reference rejects more than 2048 active total DOFs before allocation.
Invalid inputs, nonpositive eigenvalues or failed field residuals raise
ValidationError; a missing gauge raises ElectricGaugeError.

fem_toolbox.solvers.piezo_harmonic.documentation: Complex, undamped piezoelectric harmonic reference with exp(+i omega t).

HarmonicPiezoelectricResult.documentation:
Complex peak phasors (not RMS) with x(t)=Re(x_hat exp(+i omega t)).

Nodal u/v/a are (nactive,3) in m, m/s, m/s²; potential (nactive,) in V.
Original residuals contain mechanical support reactions [N] and signed
electric residuals [C]; conductor charge is their negative nodal sum.
Hz and rad/s are explicit scalar fields. Arrays are immutable snapshots.

solve_harmonic_piezoelectric.parameters: mesh: Mesh, material: PiezoelectricMaterial | Sequence[PiezoelectricMaterial], density: ArrayLike, conditions: Iterable[Dirichlet], frequency_hz: float, *, backend: LinearBackend | None=None, electrodes: Sequence[Electrode] | None=None, loads: ArrayLike | None=None, prescribed: ArrayLike | None=None
solve_harmonic_piezoelectric.documentation:
Solve one undamped harmonic state, including DC (frequency_hz=0).

``backend`` is an experimental linear-backend hook; None selects SciPy.
Reduction, physical residuals and result units remain this solver's contract.

Straight Tet4/Tet10 cells carry consistent mechanical mass, no electric mass.
Topology uses homogeneous conditions/electrodes; loads and prescribed
arrays are finite real/complex (4*nactive,) in [u,phi] DOF order. Loads
are integrated force [N] and signed electric RHS [C], prescribed values
are displacement [m] and potential [V] and zero outside fixed DOFs.
Floating electrode charge Q is a -Q load on one tied potential DOF.
Support acceleration is -omega²*u_c and its inertia is included.

Additive complex infrastructure preserves LinearSystem's real contract.
The dynamic Schur matrix is K_eff-omega² M; no damping is added to hide
resonance. A diagonal energy scaling gives a dimensionless symmetric
matrix; |lambda_min|<=1e-10 is rejected as resonance/ill-conditioning,
even with zero forcing. No infinite response is returned. The dense
2048-total-DOF bound and modal gauge/support contract apply.

fem_toolbox.solvers.piezo_transient.documentation: Undamped average-acceleration Newmark reference for piezoelectric DAEs.

KinematicValues.documentation:
Prescribed arrays in active-node order: u [m], v [m/s], a [m/s²], phi [V].

Mechanical arrays have shape (nactive,3), potential (nactive,). Entries
outside the corresponding fixed DOFs must be zero. The caller supplies
consistent derivatives; finite jumps in prescribed u or v are unsupported.

TransientPiezoelectricResult.documentation:
Owned time histories, SI units, active-node order, no damping.

Mechanical fields and original residuals: (ntime,nactive,3); potential
and electric residual: (ntime,nactive). Residual_u includes inertia and
contains support reactions. Minus residual_phi gives conductor charge
contributions; floating electrodes require summation over their nodes.
Total energy [J] is .5*v'Mv + .5*u'Kuu*u + .5*phi'D*phi, conserved for
undriven homogeneous boundaries. Residual metrics use condensed electrodes.

solve_transient_piezoelectric.parameters: mesh: Mesh, material: PiezoelectricMaterial | Sequence[PiezoelectricMaterial], density: ArrayLike, conditions: Iterable[Dirichlet], times: ArrayLike, *, backend: LinearBackend | None=None, electrodes: Sequence[Electrode] | None=None, initial_displacement: ArrayLike | None=None, initial_velocity: ArrayLike | None=None, loads: Callable[[float], ArrayLike] | None=None, prescribed: Callable[[float], KinematicValues] | None=None, events: ArrayLike=()
solve_transient_piezoelectric.documentation:
Integrate with beta=1/4, gamma=1/2, no physical or numerical damping.

``backend`` is an experimental linear-backend hook; None selects SciPy.
Reduction, physical residuals and result units remain this solver's contract.

Straight Tet4/Tet10 cells use consistent mechanical mass, no electric mass.
Topology uses homogeneous Dirichlet/electrode declarations as in modes.
loads(t) returns integrated signed [force (N), electric RHS (C)] of shape
(4*nactive,); for total floating conductor charge Q put -Q on one of its
potential DOFs. Contributions on tied nodes sum. No implicit volume/area
integration is performed. prescribed(t) supplies KinematicValues, including
voltage values on fixed potential DOFs. Defaults are all zero.

Initial u/v have shape (nactive,3) and must match supports to 1e-12 SI;
omitted arrays equal the prescribed state. Electric potential and mechanical
acceleration are solved consistently at t0, never independent initial data.
Every load/voltage jump or measured-curve knot must be listed in events [s];
interior events are inserted. Integration uses the left limit at an interval
end; stored potential/acceleration are the right-continuous state. u and v
remain continuous. Step/Ramp/TimeSeries may be used inside load callbacks;
pass their knots as events. Smooth callbacks are sampled at the grid only.

At most 2048 active DOFs and 2,000,000 stored scalar state entries; arrays
are retained in memory. Invalid data and failed residuals raise ValidationError.

fem_toolbox.solvers.piezoelectric.documentation: Monolithic quasistatic piezoelectric Tet4/Tet10 reference solver.

piezoelectric_dofs.documentation: Return field-major [u (m), phi (V)] DOFs on sorted active Tet4/Tet10 nodes.

PiezoelectricResult.documentation:
Raw monolithic solution and physical checks in active-node/cell order.

Nodal displacement is (nactive,3) m and potential (nactive,) V; cell fields
follow stress-charge SI units. Tet4 fields are constant (field_points=None);
Tet10 fields are centroid samples at field_points (ncells,3) in m. All
energy arrays are volume integrals in J, not centroid approximations.
Reactions and residuals belong to the
original signed equations, with mechanical rows in N and electric rows in
C. ``electrode_charges`` is the negative electric residual on fixed and
floating electrode nodes; ``electrode_states`` sums these by conductor.
Fieldwise relative residuals use independent backward-error denominators.
``mechanical_scale`` and ``electric_scale`` are positive characteristic
diagonal block values in N/m and C/V; they equal 1 when scaling is off.

total_enthalpy.documentation: Integrated electric enthalpy in J, not positive stored energy.

solve_piezoelectric.parameters: mesh: Mesh, material: PiezoelectricMaterial | Sequence[PiezoelectricMaterial], conditions: Iterable[Dirichlet], *, backend: LinearBackend | None=None, body_force: VectorField=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), tractions: Mapping[int, VectorField] | None=None, point_loads: Mapping[int, ArrayLike] | None=None, volume_charge: ChargeDensity=0.0, surface_charges: Mapping[int, ChargeDensity] | None=None, electrodes: Sequence[Electrode] | None=None, expansion: ThermalExpansion | Sequence[ThermalExpansion] | None=None, temperature: ArrayLike | None=None, electric_thermal_strain: bool=False, block_scaling: bool=True, method: str='direct'
solve_piezoelectric.documentation:
Solve the symmetric-indefinite static u-phi Tet4/Tet10 system with sparse LU.

``backend`` is an experimental linear-backend hook; None selects SciPy.
Reduction, physical residuals and result units remain this solver's contract.

Dirichlet DOFs use ``piezoelectric_dofs(mesh)`` and retain their original
signed reactions. Mechanical loads are N/m³, N/m², and nodal N;
``volume_charge`` is C/m³ and ``surface_charges`` prescribe outward D.n
in C/m² on exterior triangle rows. A potential reference and sufficient
mechanical supports are required on every disconnected component.
``expansion`` and nodal absolute temperature must be supplied together.
Fixed electrodes share a prescribed potential; floating electrodes share
an unknown potential and prescribe their total adjacent conductor charge.
The optional thermal-electric contribution to D is explicitly selected.
Tet10 interpolates nodal temperature at every integration point for thermal
loads and enthalpy; field values are sampled at the centroid. Straight Tet10
geometry and Triangle6 faces are required.
The only supported method is direct LU: CG is invalid for this saddle
system; MINRES awaits a verified block preconditioner. Invalid inputs,
missing constraints, singularity, or excessive field residuals raise
ValidationError (ElectricGaugeError for a missing potential reference).

fem_toolbox.solvers.piezoelectric_elemen.documentation: Internal static Tet4/Tet10 piezo dispatch with integrated enthalpy terms.

fem_toolbox.solvers.thermal_elements.documentation: Internal thermal element dispatch; Tet4 formulas remain the reference path.

fem_toolbox.solvers.thermomechanics.documentation: Sequential stationary heat to elasticity coupling on one Tet4 or straight Tet10 mesh.

solve_thermomechanics.parameters: mesh: Mesh, thermal_material: ThermalMaterial | Sequence[ThermalMaterial], elastic_material: ElasticMaterial | Sequence[ElasticMaterial], expansion: ThermalExpansion | Sequence[ThermalExpansion], thermal_conditions: Iterable[Dirichlet], mechanical_conditions: Iterable[Dirichlet], *, thermal_backend: LinearBackend | None=None, mechanical_backend: LinearBackend | None=None, source: ScalarField=0.0, outward_fluxes: Mapping[int, ScalarField] | None=None, convection: Mapping[int, Convection] | None=None, body_force: VectorField=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), tractions: Mapping[int, VectorField] | None=None, point_loads: Mapping[int, ArrayLike] | None=None
solve_thermomechanics.documentation:
Solve heat then mechanics, transferring absolute nodal K on the same mesh.

Optional thermal_backend/mechanical_backend select independent linear
backends; None uses SciPy. Coupling is one-way, stationary, without thermal
feedback from deformation. Tet10 interpolates all ten nodal temperatures
in the eigenstrain integral; mechanical energy is integrated independently.

fem_toolbox.solvers.thermopiezoelectric.documentation: One-way stationary heat transfer into the monolithic piezoelectric system.

ThermopiezoelectricResult.documentation: Thermal and coupled results, each with its own residuals and SI balances.

solve_thermopiezoelectric.parameters: mesh: Mesh, thermal_material: ThermalMaterial | Sequence[ThermalMaterial], piezoelectric_material: PiezoelectricMaterial | Sequence[PiezoelectricMaterial], expansion: ThermalExpansion | Sequence[ThermalExpansion], thermal_conditions: Iterable[Dirichlet], piezoelectric_conditions: Iterable[Dirichlet], *, thermal_backend: LinearBackend | None=None, piezoelectric_backend: LinearBackend | None=None, source: ScalarField=0.0, outward_fluxes: Mapping[int, ScalarField] | None=None, convection: Mapping[int, Convection] | None=None, body_force: VectorField=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), tractions: Mapping[int, VectorField] | None=None, point_loads: Mapping[int, ArrayLike] | None=None, volume_charge: ChargeDensity=0.0, surface_charges: Mapping[int, ChargeDensity] | None=None, electrodes: Sequence[Electrode] | None=None, electric_thermal_strain: bool=False, block_scaling: bool=True, method: str='direct'
solve_thermopiezoelectric.documentation:
Solve heat first, then transfer absolute nodal K on the same Tet4/Tet10 mesh.

Expansion is defined per cell in global engineering-Voigt order (1/K)
with a reference temperature (K). ``electric_thermal_strain`` controls
the optional thermal contribution to electric displacement explicitly.
Separate optional thermal_backend/piezoelectric_backend hooks select linear
backends (None uses SciPy). There is no reciprocal heat feedback or time dependence.

fem_toolbox.solvers.transient_heat.documentation: Backward-Euler Tet4/Tet10 heat reference with storage and reservoir reactions.

TemperatureBC.documentation: Mesh node indices with one prescribed history in K (not global DOFs).

TransientConvection.documentation: Uniform facet coefficient W/(m² K) and ambient K, optionally time-varying.

HeatFrame.documentation:
A stored time state: temperature K, gradient K/m, heat_flux W/m².

temperature/reactions/residual use active node order; element fields use
input cell order. Tet4 element fields are constant (field_points=None).
Tet10 fields are raw centroid samples; field_points (ncells,3) locates them
in metres. Initial reactions/residual are zero (not evaluated).

HeatBalance.documentation: Per-step powers in W; stored_energy_change in J relative to initial T.

TransientHeatResult.documentation:
Complete time grid; retained output frames; probes (ntime,nprobe) in K.

Probes and balances are recorded at every integration step, independently
of output_every. node_ids maps frame nodal arrays to zero-based mesh nodes.

heat_mesh_fingerprint.documentation: Hash ordered geometry/topology to prevent exporting fields on another mesh.

solve_transient_heat.parameters: mesh: Mesh, material: ThermalMaterial | Sequence[ThermalMaterial], times: ArrayLike, initial_temperature: ArrayLike, *, backend: LinearBackend | None=None, conditions: Sequence[TemperatureBC]=(), source: SpaceTimeField=0.0, outward_fluxes: Mapping[int, SpaceTimeField] | None=None, convection: Mapping[int, TransientConvection] | None=None, probes: Mapping[str, int | ArrayLike] | None=None, lumped: bool=False, lumping: Lumping | None=None, output_every: int=1, max_history_bytes: int=256 * 1024 * 1024, on_frame: Callable[[HeatFrame], None] | None=None
solve_transient_heat.documentation:
Solve C Tdot + K T = f by backward Euler on an event-enriched time grid.

``backend`` is an experimental linear-backend hook; None selects SciPy.
Reduction, physical residuals and result units remain this solver's contract.

Straight Tet10 uses consistent capacity by default; lumping="hrz" selects
conservative diagonal scaling. Tet10 rejects lumped=True (negative row-sum
masses). Tet4 retains its boolean lumped option and rejects explicit lumping.
HRZ conserves total storage but does not preserve consistent source moments.

SI: time s, initial_temperature K (scalar or active-node vector), source
W/m³, outward flux W/m². Spatial sources/fluxes may be f(x,t); explicitly
include their discontinuities in times. Profile knots are inserted for
Step/Ramp/TimeSeries. Loads use the left limit at the interval endpoint;
Dirichlet histories are right-continuous. No artificial thermal reference
is imposed on insulated components. Positive rho/c required per cell.

The initial state must match t0 Dirichlet values (1e-10 K absolute
tolerance); it is never projected silently. Full residuals include C dT/dt.
Output includes first/final frames and every output_every step; optional
on_frame permits incremental export. max_history_bytes bounds estimated
retained numerical history, not factorization/workspace memory.

fem_toolbox.studies.documentation: Versioned, local stationary parameter studies with verified result reuse.

Study.documentation:
A detached schema-1 manifest; input files are reread on each resolution.

``manifest`` has study_schema_version=1, a relative TOML ``model`` path,
and ``parameters`` (name, target, SI unit, finite nonempty values). Parameters
form a Cartesian product in declaration order (last parameter varies fastest).
Targets address existing whole properties, e.g. boundary.dirichlet.0.value.
``root`` is the manifest directory; the base model must stay inside it.
Schema/IO errors raise ModelSchemaError. Physical case errors are recorded by
run(). No expressions, transient models, remote execution or new meshing.

__init__.parameters: self, manifest: Mapping[str, object], *, root: str | Path

from_file.documentation: Read a UTF-8 .toml manifest with paths relative to its directory.

resolve.documentation:
Return detached deterministic case records, without solving any model.

Case IDs hash named parameter values/units/targets; input fingerprints
additionally cover complete model data, mesh bytes, scale, explicit
solver settings, schema/toolbox/dependency versions and study revision.
A changed base input invalidates reuse while retaining the case ID.

run.parameters: self, output: str | Path, *, max_cases: int | None=None
run.documentation:
Run/retry cases serially and return the persisted schema-1 catalog.

``max_cases`` limits newly attempted cases, not cached successes. None
runs all cases. Case exceptions are persisted and subsequent cases run;
KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit persist ``interrupted`` and are re-raised.
Catalog/locking errors propagate. A lock prevents concurrent writers;
after a hard process kill remove .study.lock only after checking no
writer remains. Partial attempt directories are retained, never reused.

fem_toolbox.study_reports.documentation: Deterministic SI quantity tables and reports from stored stationary studies.

Quantity.documentation:
One scalar output definition; indices are global nodes or volume-cell rows.

Metric fields use dotted bundle paths (e.g. heat.power_balance_W). Point/cell
fields use exported array names. Select a vector component by its metadata
name or 'norm'. No selection means all active nodes/volume cells; no padding
or smoothing. scalar requires exactly one selected value. Tolerances, if
supplied, evaluate abs(value) <= tolerance in this quantity's SI unit.

export_study_table.parameters: catalog_path: str | Path, output: str | Path, quantities: Sequence[Quantity]
export_study_table.documentation:
Write values.csv, metadata.json and report.md into a new output directory.

All active catalog cases are retained; unavailable quantities are null with
reasons, encoded as empty CSV cells. Existing directories are never replaced.
Invalid bundles remain visible; models are never solved. Returned path points
to metadata.json. A failed write can leave an incomplete directory, which
must not be consumed until metadata.json and the CSV hash validate.

read_study_table.documentation:
Read schema-1 metadata and verify the matching CSV, without FEM execution.

Raises ValueError for unsupported/corrupt data, OSError for missing files.
Returned JSON data includes column contracts, per-case values and provenance.

fem_toolbox.surrogates.documentation:
Inspectable polynomial surrogates for real scalar FEM quantities.

No FEM solve, ML dependency, hyperparameter search or uncertainty claim is made.
All arrays use sample rows and explicitly ordered parameter/output columns.

Variable.documentation: Explicit column identity, SI unit and physical definition (no conversion).

SurrogateData.documentation:
Validated owned data X[n,p], Y[n,q], IDs and mandatory source provenance.

X/Y must be finite real matrices, never complex/bool/object or empty. Data
and metadata are detached from caller mutation; array storage is read-only.
Every row needs a unique nonempty case ID. Units are explicit SI declarations,
not a unit-conversion engine. Raises ValueError for incompatible data.

__init__.parameters: self, X: ArrayLike, Y: ArrayLike, case_ids: Sequence[str], parameters: Sequence[Variable], targets: Sequence[Variable], *, provenance: Mapping[str, object]

from_table.parameters: cls, directory: str | Path, *, parameter_columns: Sequence[str], target_columns: Sequence[str], exclude_invalid: bool=False
from_table.documentation:
Load selected scalar columns from a verified #60 CSV/JSON table.

Failed/unavailable cases, explicitly failed balance checks and missing,
nonfinite or nonscalar selected values are rejected by default. Explicit
exclusion records every excluded case and all reasons in provenance.
Unchecked balances remain visibly unchecked, never promoted to passed.

X.documentation: Read-only parameters in declared SI units, shape [n,p].

Y.documentation: Read-only targets in declared SI units, shape [n,q].

provenance.documentation: Detached source metadata, including any table exclusion log.

fingerprint.documentation: SHA-256 of values, row/column identity, definitions and provenance.

DataSplit.documentation: Explicit train/test ID partition; seed records optional random splitting.

split_cases.parameters: data: SurrogateData, *, test_fraction: float, seed: int
split_cases.documentation:
Seeded split of distinct X groups; duplicate inputs always stay together.

Fraction applies to groups, rounded up, with at least one group on each side.
Order within each side follows the original dataset. No fitting is performed.

Prediction.documentation: Values [n,q] in target units and an outside-training-box flag per row.

PolynomialSurrogate.documentation:
Polynomial fitted by fit_surrogate; prediction needs only its artifact.

Min/max checks are box checks, not guarantees of accuracy inside the box.
Test errors are empirical errors, never uncertainty intervals/error bounds.

__init__.parameters: self, document: Mapping[str, Any]

report.documentation: Detached training/test errors, split, source and version provenance.

to_document.documentation: Return an inspectable detached JSON document.

save.parameters: self, path: str | Path, *, overwrite: bool=False
save.documentation:
Atomically save schema-1 JSON/checksum; default refuses overwriting.

Parent must exist. No pickle, executable data or training files required.
Overwrite uses atomic replacement; exclusive publication uses a hard link.

load.documentation:
Validate checksum, version and complete model structure from JSON.

Raises ValueError for damaged/incompatible artifacts; filesystem errors
propagate. A checksum detects accidental damage, not hostile tampering.

predict.documentation:
Predict one [p] or several [n,p] points; always return [n,q] values.

Outside-box input raises ValueError by default. Explicit permission
returns per-row flags. Columns must follow the exposed parameter order.
Complex, nonfinite, empty and dimensionally incompatible arrays fail.

fit_surrogate.parameters: data: SurrogateData, split: DataSplit, *, degree: int=1, ridge: float=0.0
fit_surrogate.documentation:
Fit total-degree 1/2 polynomial with train-only box scaling and intercept.

Ridge solves ||A B - Y||² + ridge*||B[1:]||² by augmented least squares;
intercept is unpenalized. No normal equations or automatic tuning. At least
as many distinct training points as basis terms are required, even for ridge.
Constant parameters are rejected (remove them explicitly); constant outputs
are allowed. Unregularized rank deficiency raises ValueError. Test data is
used only for the returned evaluation report, never scaling or fitting.

fem_toolbox.time.documentation: Deterministic SI time grids and scalar prescribed histories (no expressions).

Step.documentation: Right-continuous scalar step; time in s, before/after in caller's SI unit.

Ramp.documentation:
Linear ramp on [start,end] s, held constant before and after.

Finite ordered time limits and finite scalar amplitudes are required.
Overflowing intermediate spans are normalized; exact endpoints and constant
amplitudes are retained. This does not extend a solver's time-grid support.

TimeSeries.documentation:
Immutable measured scalar samples. Times in seconds, values in stated SI unit.

Linear interpolation is default; previous is right-continuous zero-order
hold. Extrapolation defaults to error; hold must be selected explicitly.
Duplicate/nonfinite times, nonfinite values and unknown modes are rejected.

__init__.parameters: self, times: ArrayLike, values: ArrayLike, *, interpolation: Literal['linear', 'previous']='linear', extrapolation: Literal['error', 'hold']='error', unit: str='1'

from_csv.parameters: cls, path: str | Path, *, value_column: str, unit: str, time_column: str='time_s', delimiter: str=',', interpolation: Literal['linear', 'previous']='linear', extrapolation: Literal['error', 'hold']='error'
from_csv.documentation: Read numeric UTF-8 CSV columns, explicitly in s and the given SI unit.

signal_value.parameters: signal: TimeSignal, time: float, *, side: Side='right'
signal_value.documentation: Evaluate a finite scalar history at a specified side of an event.

integration_times.documentation: Validate times and insert all interior signal knots, without rounding.

fem_toolbox.topology.documentation:
Filtered SIMP design for stationary Tet4 elasticity; SI and fixed dead loads.

The reference implementation delegates every state to the verified elasticity
solver. It is intentionally limited to small, deterministic local studies.

LoadCase.documentation:
Named homogeneous supports and density-independent SI forces.

conditions use mechanical_dofs(mesh). body_force is N/m³, tractions map
Triangle3 rows to N/m², point_loads map mesh nodes to N. No callable loads.

DensityEvaluation.documentation: Densities/gradients in input-cell order; compliance J, volume fraction 1.

TopologyProblem.documentation:
Volume-weighted linear density filter and SIMP on a fixed Tet4 mesh.

Variables have shape (ncells,), fixed values included. Radius is metres;
weights are positive, not implicitly normalized. Materials are homogeneous
or one immutable positive tensor per cell. No projection or continuation.

__init__.parameters: self, mesh: Mesh, material: ElasticMaterial | Sequence[ElasticMaterial], cases: Sequence[LoadCase], *, filter_radius: float, weights: ArrayLike | None=None, fixed_solid: ArrayLike=(), fixed_void: ArrayLike=(), penalty: float=3.0, minimum_stiffness: float=0.001

from_models.parameters: cls, models: Sequence[Model], *, weights: ArrayLike | None=None, **options: Any
from_models.documentation: Share the validated Model parser; reject different meshes/materials.

physical_density.documentation: Map bounded design variables to physical densities, no threshold.

evaluate.documentation: Solve independent load states and exact filtered compliance gradients.

initial_density.documentation: Find feasible uniform free variables including fixed/filter effects.

fem_toolbox.topology_geometry.documentation: Thresholded Tet4 geometry and independent full-material elastic reanalysis.

GeometryResult.documentation: Exact selected-cell geometry with unchanged dead loads and full material.

maximum_von_mises_Pa.documentation: Largest raw cell stress among all cases, not an allowable stress.

to_record.documentation: Predeclared compliance/volume gate and diagnostic cell indices.

reanalyze_geometry.parameters: problem: TopologyProblem, field: DensityEvaluation, threshold: float, *, connect: bool=False
reanalyze_geometry.documentation:
Keep rho>=threshold, reject disconnected solids or removed loaded faces.

Newly exposed surfaces are traction-free. Prescribed support components are
remapped onto retained active nodes; the original solver checks rigid modes.
Body forces on removed volume are rejected rather than silently changed.

export_reanalyses.parameters: problem: TopologyProblem, field: DensityEvaluation, output: str | Path, thresholds: tuple[float, ...]=(0.25, 0.35, 0.45)
export_reanalyses.documentation: Export every valid geometry; retain explicit No-go records for others.

fem_toolbox.topology_optimization.documentation: Bounded, deterministic SLSQP driver for filtered SIMP compliance.

OptimizationOptions.documentation: Iteration/design-evaluation budgets and dimensionless SLSQP tolerance.

OptimizationResult.documentation:
Final feasible state, explicit stop status and accepted-step diagnostics.

A budget stop retains the best feasible state without claiming convergence.
Each history row contains SI compliance, fraction, residual and step change.

optimize_topology.parameters: problem: TopologyProblem, volume_fraction: float, *, initial: ArrayLike | None=None, options: OptimizationOptions | None=None
optimize_topology.documentation:
Minimize weighted compliance with exact filter gradients and SI states.

Invalid configurations raise ValidationError. Numerical failures during the
search return solver_failed with the last best feasible state and message.
The initial solve itself must succeed; no invalid result is fabricated.

fem_toolbox.topology_study.documentation: Declarative local topology studies with immutable-input and artifact hashes.

problem_document.documentation: Detached effective SI inputs; no hidden Model parsing or host paths.

TopologyStudy.documentation: One explicit local optimization; output directories must be new.

__init__.parameters: self, problem: TopologyProblem, volume_fraction: float, *, options: OptimizationOptions | None=None

from_file.documentation: Load schema-1 TOML referencing existing static Model TOML files.

run.documentation:
Optimize and save schema-1 JSON/VTU plus SHA-256 inventory.

Budget/solver status is preserved; no stopped state becomes successful.
Invalid initial states raise before an output directory is created.

read_topology_result.documentation: Read a schema-1 result only after verifying all bound artifact bytes.

fem_toolbox.transient_model.documentation: Additive model schema 2 for transient heat; schema 1 remains stationary.

resolve_csv_profiles.documentation: Embed CSV samples in a detached document; only files under model root.

__init__.parameters: self, mesh: Mesh, document: Mapping[str, Any]

solve.documentation: Solve with model/document and material-source provenance included.

fem_toolbox.uncertainty.documentation:
Explicit Monte Carlo input uncertainty, separate from numerical model errors.

Laws describe user assumptions, never inferred measurement distributions. Rows
are joint samples, columns follow parameter declaration order. No optimizer,
inverse identification or experimental validation is performed.

Normal.documentation:
Unbounded normal law with finite mean and positive standard deviation.

Values are in the parameter's declared SI unit. Negative/otherwise
unphysical samples are not clipped; a model may reject them explicitly.

Uniform.documentation:
Uniform probability law on a finite increasing SI interval.

An interval alone does not justify a uniform law; the caller must state
why this probability assumption is appropriate for the intended study.

UncertainParameter.documentation: Scalar M8 target, explicit SI unit, law and mandatory justification.

SamplingPlan.documentation:
Detached joint Monte Carlo specification with PCG64 and explicit seed.

``size`` is an integer >=2, ``seed`` a nonnegative integer. Default inputs
are independent. An optional real correlation[p,p] must be symmetric, PSD
and have unit diagonal (absolute roundoff tolerance 1e-12). Nonidentity
correlation is supported only for all-normal inputs. Singular normal
correlation is valid; eigenvalues in [-1e-12,0] are rounded to zero.
``sample`` returns immutable float64 rows [size,p], detached from callers.
No distribution fitting, truncation or automatic unit conversion.

__init__.parameters: self, parameters: Sequence[UncertainParameter], *, size: int, seed: int, correlation: ArrayLike | None=None

to_document.documentation: Return detached schema-1 provenance, including laws and RNG method.

sample.documentation: Generate joint samples; same specification/runtime gives same bytes.

summarize_samples.parameters: values: ArrayLike, *, unit: str, numerical_error_bound: float | None, quantile_probabilities: Sequence[float]=(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)
summarize_samples.documentation:
Summarize finite real output rows; never omit failed/nonfinite samples.

Variance is unbiased (ddof=1); quantiles use NumPy linear interpolation.
Quantile bands are output probability estimates, not confidence intervals
or guaranteed bounds. Prefix moments document sample convergence, not a
proof that sampling error is negligible. ``numerical_error_bound`` is an
externally justified deterministic bound in ``unit``, or None if unknown;
it is reported separately and is never added to statistical variance.

local_sensitivity.parameters: evaluate: Callable[[NDArray[np.float64]], float], *, center: ArrayLike, steps: ArrayLike
local_sensitivity.documentation:
Central finite-difference gradient at explicit SI center and positive steps.

Each derivative has output-unit/input-unit; it is local, not a global
variance decomposition. The caller must establish step convergence and
admissibility of center +/- step. Callback exceptions propagate. Exactly
2*p scalar evaluations; callback inputs are detached copies.

UncertaintyStudy.documentation:
Joint scalar sampling on the public stationary M8 Study/Quantity APIs.

The relative ``model`` TOML and its mesh must remain inside ``root``. Each
joint row runs as a one-case Study, so correlations are retained without a
Cartesian product. M8 owns validation, retry, provenance and hashed result
reuse. Reusing an output directory requires identical sampling provenance;
changed model/mesh bytes invalidate cached M8 results. Normal-law physical
failures stay visible and suppress all uncertainty statistics (no silent
clipping or conditional subset). Results are not an experimental claim.

__init__.parameters: self, plan: SamplingPlan, *, model: str, root: str | Path

run.parameters: self, output: str | Path, *, quantities: Sequence[Quantity], numerical_error_bounds: Mapping[str, float | None], sensitivity_center: ArrayLike | None=None, sensitivity_steps: ArrayLike | None=None
run.documentation:
Write sampling.json and atomic uncertainty.json; return detached data.

Every quantity requires an explicit deterministic numerical-error bound
in its SI unit or None (unknown), never a default zero. Optional local
sensitivities require center[p] and positive steps[p] together; each
quantity derivative uses its output unit divided by the input unit.
Caller establishes admissibility and step convergence. Sensitivities
are suppressed if a perturbation fails; sampling statistics may still
be complete. Tables/case receipts and fingerprints remain inspectable.

An exclusive lock rejects concurrent writers. Interrupted case runs
retain their M8 recovery state; rerunning resumes successes. After a
hard kill, verify no writer remains before manually removing the lock.
Schema errors propagate, physical failures appear in the report.
